title: BloombergNEF’s Transition Metals Outlook 2026: Global Metal Supply Shortages Set to Ease, but Copper Faces a $332 Billion Investment Gap | BloombergNEF
gist: BNEF's Transition Metals Outlook 2026 says nine of 10 transition materials now have sufficient supply through 2050, with LFP adoption cutting cobalt/nickel demand and oversupply pressuring prices for several metals. Copper is the exception: a deficit from 2028 widening to 20Mt (44% of demand) by 2050, requiring $332bn in new mines that take ~17 years to build. China's refining dominance and DRC/Indonesia policy remain supply-security risks.

insights.claim: BNEF forecasts a copper supply deficit starting in 2028 that widens to 20 million metric tons by 2050, equal to 44% of projected global demand.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Copper is the one transition metal where BNEF sees a durable, widening shortfall — the core long-copper thesis.
insights.quote: BNEF forecasts a supply deficit beginning in 2028 and widening to 20 million metric tons by 2050 – equivalent to 44% of projected global demand.

insights.claim: Closing the copper gap would require about $332 billion of investment in new mines.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Sizes the capex wave miners must fund; underinvestment implies price-led rationing instead.
insights.quote: require $332 billion of investment in new mines

insights.claim: Because new copper mines take an average of 17 years to come online, the deficit could persist for decades even if the required investment is made.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Supply response is too slow to cap prices this cycle; the shortage is not solvable by capital alone in the near term.
insights.quote: bringing new mines into operation takes an average of 17 years, meaning the shortfall could persist for decades

insights.claim: Declining ore grades and years of underinvestment in exploration compound copper's supply challenge.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Rising cost curves for existing producers support higher marginal-cost pricing.

insights.claim: Copper demand is expected to rise 61% between 2026 and 2050 to almost 46 million tons, with electrified-transport use alone up 244% to 11.4 million tons.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: EVs and grids are the marginal demand drivers; electrified transport becomes roughly a quarter of copper demand.
insights.quote: copper use in electrified transport alone projected to increase by 244% to 11.4 million tons

insights.claim: A copper shortfall could raise prices, force manufacturers to substitute alternative materials and slow deployment of EVs, batteries and grids.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Second-order: copper scarcity is a brake on electrification and a tailwind for substitutes such as aluminium.

insights.claim: BNEF now expects nine of the 10 transition materials it studies to have sufficient supply capacity through 2050, versus three materials projected in deficit in last year's outlook.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: The 'critical minerals shortage' narrative is largely over except for copper — a contrarian read against scarcity-premium valuations.
insights.quote: This marks an improvement on last year’s outlook, when three materials were projected to face deficits.
insights.locator: The outlook for metals has improved

insights.claim: Graphite, platinum and steel have shifted from projected deficits to surpluses compared with last year's outlook.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Rapid forecast reversals show how fast supply response erodes scarcity theses.
insights.locator: Oversupply could put pressure on prices

insights.claim: The sufficiency of supply is conditional on producers continuing to develop mines and replace depleted reserves.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: If oversupply-driven capex cuts happen, today's comfortable outlook can flip back to deficit.
insights.locator: The outlook for metals has improved

insights.claim: Martin Tengler argues the challenge has shifted from whether the world can produce enough metals overall to whether the right materials will be available when and where they are needed.
insights.speaker: Martin Tengler
insights.so_what: Value shifts from volume to location, timing and supply security — favoring secure, diversified supply chains.
insights.quote: The challenge now is less about whether the world can produce enough metals overall, and more about whether the right materials will be available when and where they are needed.
insights.locator: Martin Tengler, Head of Metals and Mining

insights.claim: Lithium demand is forecast to nearly triple to 4.8 million metric tons LCE by 2050 from 1.6 million tons in 2026, driven by EVs and energy storage.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Volume growth is strong, but BNEF simultaneously expects long-term lithium price pressure — volume does not equal price upside.
insights.locator: Lithium demand is forecast to nearly triple

insights.claim: Graphite demand is set to more than double to 6.9 million metric tons by 2050 from 3.3 million.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Demand growth coexists with a projected surplus, limiting pricing power.
insights.locator: Lithium demand is forecast to nearly triple

insights.claim: Growing adoption of lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries has reduced BNEF's projected demand for cobalt and nickel versus prior editions.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Chemistry shifts structurally impair cobalt and nickel demand theses tied to NMC batteries.
insights.quote: the growing adoption of lithium iron phosphate batteries has reduced BNEF’s projected demand for cobalt and nickel

insights.claim: BNEF expects long-term downward price pressure on cobalt, lithium, manganese, nickel and palladium, potentially prompting miners to cut costs, limit production or close capacity.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Bearish for producers of these metals; capacity closures could later seed the next deficit cycle.
insights.locator: Oversupply could put pressure on prices

insights.claim: Eight of the 10 materials studied have more than half their refining capacity concentrated in a single country, and seven of those are concentrated in China.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Geopolitical leverage sits in midstream refining, not mining — supporting non-China refining build-out and policy support.
insights.quote: Eight of the 10 materials studied have more than half their refining capacity concentrated in a single country; seven of these are in China.

insights.claim: Government restrictions on cobalt exports from the Democratic Republic of Congo and on nickel production in Indonesia could constrain availability despite the long-term surplus picture.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Resource nationalism can override surplus fundamentals and create policy-driven price spikes.

insights.claim: Lithium faces a temporary deficit that is expected to ease as new capacity comes online in 2027, while palladium's deficit is projected to persist until around 2034.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Near-term lithium tightness is a trade, not a structural story; palladium tightness is longer-dated.

insights.claim: Six of the 10 materials studied will require recycling to meet projected demand by 2035, rising to eight by 2050.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Recycling becomes a necessary supply source, not an ESG add-on — a growth market for metals recyclers.
insights.quote: Six of the 10 materials studied will require recycling to meet projected demand by 2035, rising to eight by 2050.
